See the whole library in use at birdalbum.com . Bird Album is a free bird guide built on these stickers: look up any species by name in 15 languages, see where it lives and which months it is around, and open a map of 8,171 birding hotspots that shows what people are seeing at each one this month.
By Huashu (花叔) , from the bird-watching app Mingji (鸣迹). 11,064 bird species, one sticker each, across 44 orders and 250 families: every living species in the IOC World Bird List v15.2 (the 163 extinct species are not included). Each species comes with structured data: taxonomy, names in up to 43 languages, cross-database IDs, and where every sticker came from.
License in short: use the stickers for anything, including commercial work, editing and redistribution. The one exception is a birding, bird-ID or field-guide app, site or service. Credit huashu-bird-sticker with a link to this repository and you're set. The legal text is PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 . The data is MIT, and third-party parts are listed in NOTICE .
Eighteen of the most colourful and distinctive groups, 24 stickers each, picked so that no two look alike. Every sticker shown here meets the quality bar.

A record looks like this (names shortened):
Names: English covers every species, French and Simplified Chinese all but a handful (Simplified Chinese has no names yet for 23 recently split species); Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Russian, German, Spanish, Polish, Dutch, Swedish and about a dozen more European languages cover over 90%. Serbian, Hungarian and Estonian are between 50% and 75%. Korean, Arabic, Thai, Persian and some others cover only a few hundred to about a thousand species so far, because that is what the IOC list has. See data/names.csv .
IDs: Wikidata 10,939, GBIF 10,649, eBird 10,052.
How the stickers were made, and how good they are
11,064 stickers are AI illustrations. For each species we found a reference photo (or, for 453 species where no single photo was good enough, a board of several images plus a written description), drew the sticker with GPT-image, upscaled it, and cut it out.
Every AI sticker was then scored by a separate reviewer against the reference for field marks: bill, eye, legs and feet, plumage pattern and colour. In the last round, 852 borderline stickers (80–82) also got a second, blind review, and 211 of them failed it and were redrawn. Borderline stickers from earlier rounds did not get this second review.
7,668 meet our quality bar ( "meetsQualityBar": true ): AI stickers scoring 80 or above.
3,396 do not. They were redrawn up to the limit, and we kept the best-scoring version so that no species is left without a picture. 3,281 score 70–79, 109 score below 70, and 6 scored 80+ but failed the blind second review.
These are illustrations, not field-guide plates. Treat them as a friendly picture of the bird, and check a field guide before relying on a fine detail. If you spot a mistake, please open an issue — corrections from birders are the most valuable contribution this project can get.
Every sticker is a new AI drawing, and no reference photo is included in this repository. The image each species was drawn from (page, author and license) is recorded in sticker.reference in data/species.json , so every sticker can be traced back to its source. A breakdown by reference license is in data/README.md .
The repository is about 700 MB. To fetch only the data and a few stickers:
Taxonomy and multilingual names: IOC World Bird List v15.2, Gill, Donsker & Rasmussen (Eds), CC BY 3.0.
Body measurements and ecology: AVONET, Tobias et al. 2022, Ecology Letters , CC BY 4.0.
Reference photographers: credited per species in data/species.json . Reference photos are not included in this repository.
Stickers drawn for 鸣迹 (Mingji), a bird-watching notebook app for iOS.
If a sticker is based on your photo and you would rather it weren't, open an issue or email alchaincyf@gmail.com and we will replace or remove it within 7 days.
